label: East Asian mansion
summary: The game concept East Asian Mansion: a domicile held by the house head of a notable noble family in the Japanese administrative and feudal realms.
details: `[east_asian_estate|E]` in a text shows East Asian Mansion, linked to the concept's explanation. It stands for private land not tied to any landed title. Buildings can be added to it to grow the family's wealth and influence, and it passes to later generations. Vanilla uses it in the concept texts of the mansion and its buildings.

label: East Asian mansion building
summary: The game concept East Asian Mansion Building: a lasting improvement built at an East Asian mansion.
details: `[east_asian_estate_building|E]` in a text shows East Asian Mansion Building, linked to the concept's explanation. The mansion's owner can build many kinds of them to earn private income, grow the family's influence and get access to decisions, interactions and more. Vanilla's texts do not use this key.

label: East Asian mansion buildings
summary: The plural form of the game concept East Asian Mansion Building, shown as the words East Asian Mansion Buildings.
details: `[east_asian_estate_buildings|E]` in a text shows East Asian Mansion Buildings, linked to the explanation of these lasting improvements to a mansion. Vanilla's texts do not use this key.

label: East Asian mansions
summary: The plural form of the game concept East Asian Mansion, shown as the words East Asian Mansions.
details: `[east_asian_estates|E]` in a text shows East Asian Mansions, linked to the explanation of these family domiciles of Japan's noble families. Vanilla's texts do not use this key.

label: Eastern Roman Empire
summary: The game concept Eastern Roman Empire: an empire title that the holder of the Roman Empire can create.
details: `[eastern_roman_empire|E]` in a text shows Eastern Roman Empire, linked to the concept's explanation. It is created by taking the decision that splits the Roman Empire. Vanilla uses it in that decision's texts (the realm is split in two, and the new holder gets the Eastern Roman Empire).

label: Conservative
summary: A short alias of the game concept Conservative (at an ecumenical council), shown as the word Conservative.
details: `[ec_conservative|E]` in a text shows Conservative, linked to the explanation: guests of an ecumenical council who vote against the host's proposals to change the status of a core tenet or a doctrine, opposed by the innovators. Only clergy, rulers with a clerical puppet and the host may vote. Vanilla uses it in council events where a character switches sides.

label: Conservatives
summary: A short plural alias of the game concept Conservative (at an ecumenical council), shown as the word Conservatives.
details: `[ec_conservatives|E]` in a text shows Conservatives, linked to the explanation of the council guests who vote against changing a core tenet or doctrine. Vanilla uses it often in the council's window labels and events (75 uses through chains).

label: Innovator
summary: A short alias of the game concept Innovator (at an ecumenical council), shown as the word Innovator.
details: `[ec_innovator|E]` in a text shows Innovator, linked to the explanation: guests of an ecumenical council who vote with the host's proposals to change the status of a core tenet or a doctrine, opposed by the conservatives who want things to stay as they are. Vanilla uses it in council events where a character switches sides.

label: Innovators
summary: A short plural alias of the game concept Innovator (at an ecumenical council), shown as the word Innovators.
details: `[ec_innovators|E]` in a text shows Innovators, linked to the explanation of the council guests who vote for the host's changes. Vanilla uses it in the council's texts, for example for what happens when more than 50% are innovators at the end of the debate.

label: Beseech claim
summary: The game concept for the Beseech Claim interaction: it gets a claim on a title that belongs to another ruler.
details: `[ecclesiastic_grant_claim_interaction|E]` in a text shows the interaction's name, Beseech Claim, linked to the concept's explanation. It needs the acceptance of a relevant ecclesiastical or theocratic character. Vanilla uses it in effect texts that make this interaction more likely to be accepted.

label: Incite claim war
summary: The game concept for the Incite Claim War interaction: an ecclesiastical ruler makes a secular ruler of the same faith declare war to press a claim on another secular ruler.
details: `[ecclesiastic_incite_claim_war_interaction|E]` in a text shows the interaction's name, Incite Claim War, linked to the concept's explanation. Vanilla's texts do not use this key.

label: Incite holy war
summary: The game concept for the Incite Holy War interaction: an ecclesiastical ruler makes a secular ruler of the same faith declare a holy war on rulers of a hostile faith.
details: `[ecclesiastic_incite_holy_war_interaction|E]` in a text shows the interaction's name, Incite Holy War, linked to the concept's explanation. Vanilla uses it in a parameter text of the Christian church situation.

label: Negotiate for land
summary: The game concept for the Negotiate For Land interaction: a peaceful transfer of a title or vassal between two rulers, which needs the target ruler's and a church intercessor's acceptance.
details: `[ecclesiastic_transfer_land_interaction|E]` in a text shows the interaction's name, Negotiate For Land, linked to the concept's explanation. Refusing usually costs the recipient piety and legitimacy plus an extra cost the actor picks. The intercessor, an ecclesiastical or theocratic ruler, can forbid the interaction, and with the highest church authority law can force its acceptance. Vanilla uses it in law and trait texts.

label: Ecclesiastical
summary: The game concept Ecclesiastical: the theocratic form of government of Christian clergy rulers such as bishops and archbishops.
details: `[ecclesiastical|E]` in a text shows Ecclesiastical, linked to the concept's explanation. Most such rulers are vassals who lease their temple holdings from a secular liege and answer to the head of faith; a bishop with landed titles that are not leased can rule independently. Their power over their own vassals depends on church authority. Vanilla uses the word in many texts, such as court position salaries.

label: Ecclesiastical estate
summary: Another key of the game concept Ecclesiastical Estate: the domicile of an archbishop, tied to a clerical title.
details: `[ecclesiastical_domicile|E]` in a text shows Ecclesiastical Estate, linked to the concept's explanation. The estate (also called a cathedral complex) stands for the private lands of an archbishop and their see; lesser clergy get one only on rising to such a title. Buildings there add wealth, piety and spiritual fulfillment. It stays in place and passes to the title's next holder. Vanilla uses this key in decision and estate texts.

label: Ecclesiastical estate building
summary: Another key of the game concept Ecclesiastical Estate Building: a lasting improvement built at an ecclesiastical estate.
details: `[ecclesiastical_domicile_building|E]` in a text shows Ecclesiastical Estate Building, linked to the concept's explanation. The holder can build many kinds of them for private income, piety, spiritual fulfillment and access to decisions and interactions. Vanilla uses this key in interaction and estate texts.

label: Ecclesiastical estate
summary: Another key of the game concept Ecclesiastical Estate, shown as the words Ecclesiastical Estate: the domicile of an archbishop, tied to a clerical title.
details: `[ecclesiastical_estate|E]` in a text shows Ecclesiastical Estate, linked to the concept's explanation (the same concept as `ecclesiastical_domicile`). It does not move and passes to the title's next holder. Vanilla uses this key in the concept texts of clerical regions and estate buildings.

label: Ecclesiastical estate building
summary: Another key of the game concept Ecclesiastical Estate Building, shown as the words Ecclesiastical Estate Building.
details: `[ecclesiastical_estate_building|E]` in a text shows Ecclesiastical Estate Building, linked to the explanation of these improvements to an archbishop's estate (the same concept as `ecclesiastical_domicile_building`). Vanilla's texts do not use this key.

label: Ecclesiastical estate buildings
summary: The plural form of the game concept Ecclesiastical Estate Building, shown as the words Ecclesiastical Estate Buildings.
details: `[ecclesiastical_estate_buildings|E]` in a text shows Ecclesiastical Estate Buildings, linked to the explanation of these improvements to an archbishop's estate. Vanilla uses it in the estate's own concept text.

label: Ecclesiastical estates
summary: The plural form of the game concept Ecclesiastical Estate, shown as the words Ecclesiastical Estates.
details: `[ecclesiastical_estates|E]` in a text shows Ecclesiastical Estates, linked to the explanation of archbishops' estates. Vanilla's texts do not use this key.

label: Ecclesiastical government
summary: Another name of the game concept Ecclesiastical, shown as the words Ecclesiastical Government.
details: `[ecclesiastical_government|E]` in a text shows Ecclesiastical Government, linked to the explanation of the theocratic government of Christian clergy rulers. Vanilla uses it in succession law texts and when a character takes up this government by buying sacred land.

label: Ecclesiastical icon
summary: The ecclesiastical government icon, an alias of the game concept Ecclesiastical whose name text is the icon `@government_type_ecclesiastical!`.
details: `[ecclesiastical_i|E]` in a text shows the icon, linked to the explanation of the ecclesiastical government. Vanilla puts it in front of the word, as in the modifier name "[ecclesiastical_i|E] [ecclesiastical|E] Ruler Opinion".

label: Economic building
summary: The game concept Economic Building: a building whose main job is to raise its holding's domain income.
details: `[economic_building|E]` in a text shows Economic Building, linked to the concept's explanation. Vanilla uses it in effect texts that give a holding a random economic building.

label: Economic buildings
summary: The plural form of the game concept Economic Building, shown as the words Economic Buildings.
details: `[economic_buildings|E]` in a text shows Economic Buildings, linked to the explanation of buildings that raise domain income. Vanilla uses it in AI concept texts and in innovations that unlock them.

label: Economic archetype
summary: The game concept Economic Archetype: the AI behaviour that decides how a ruler spends their gold, based largely on their traits.
details: `[economical_archetype|E]` in a text shows Economic Archetype, linked to the concept's explanation, which lists the archetypes: warlike, cautious, economic boom, unpredictable and conqueror. Vanilla uses it in the AI personality tooltip and in a vassal interaction about building fortifications.

label: Ecumenical council
summary: The game concept Ecumenical Council: an activity in which the highest clergy of all Christendom meet to decide the Church's future.
details: `[ecumenical_council|E]` in a text shows Ecumenical Council, linked to the concept's explanation. Over several debates they decide the status of disputed core tenets (permitted, prohibited, or raised to core tenet) and settle the faith's doctrines. Vanilla uses it in the council's activity texts and message filters.

label: Conservative
summary: The game concept Conservative: a guest at an ecumenical council who votes against the host's proposals to change a core tenet or doctrine.
details: `[ecumenical_council_conservative|E]` in a text shows Conservative, linked to the concept's explanation. Conservatives stand against the innovators, who push for the changes. Only clergy, rulers with a clerical puppet and the host may vote. Vanilla's texts write the short form `ec_conservative` instead.

label: Conservatives
summary: The plural form of the game concept Conservative (at an ecumenical council), shown as the word Conservatives.
details: `[ecumenical_council_conservatives|E]` in a text shows Conservatives, linked to the explanation of the council guests who vote against changes. Vanilla's texts write the short form `ec_conservatives` instead.

label: Innovator
summary: The game concept Innovator: a guest at an ecumenical council who votes with the host's proposals to change a core tenet or doctrine.
details: `[ecumenical_council_innovator|E]` in a text shows Innovator, linked to the concept's explanation. Innovators stand against the conservatives, who want to keep things as they are. Vanilla's texts write the short form `ec_innovator` instead.

label: Innovators
summary: The plural form of the game concept Innovator (at an ecumenical council), shown as the word Innovators.
details: `[ecumenical_council_innovators|E]` in a text shows Innovators, linked to the explanation of the council guests who vote for the host's changes. Vanilla's texts write the short form `ec_innovators` instead.

label: Ecumenical councils
summary: The plural form of the game concept Ecumenical Council, shown as the words Ecumenical Councils.
details: `[ecumenical_councils|E]` in a text shows Ecumenical Councils, linked to the explanation of these gatherings of Christendom's clergy. Vanilla uses it in important action texts about manipulating councils.

label: Educate
summary: Another name of the game concept Education Focus, shown as the word Educate.
details: `[educate|E]` in a text shows Educate, linked to the explanation of a child's education focus (the skill that children aged 6 to 9 are trained in). Vanilla uses it in the guardian's concept text ("assigned to educate a child").

label: Educated
summary: Another name of the game concept Education Focus, shown as the word Educated.
details: `[educated|E]` in a text shows Educated, linked to the explanation of a child's education focus. Vanilla uses it in the ward's concept text and in an interaction text about children who can be educated.

label: Education
summary: Another name of the game concept Education Focus, shown as the word Education.
details: `[education|E]` in a text shows Education, linked to the explanation of the education focus: children aged 6 to 9 are trained towards one of the five skills and end up with an education trait at adulthood. Vanilla uses the word in building and court position texts, among others.

label: Education focus
summary: The game concept Education Focus: the skill, one of five, that a child aged 6 to 9 is trained towards.
details: `[education_focus|E]` in a text shows Education Focus, linked to the concept's explanation. The education ends with an education trait when the child becomes an adult; its quality depends on how well the childhood trait fits the focus and on the guardian's matching skill. When setting the focus you can also choose whether the child is raised in the guardian's faith and culture. Vanilla uses it in the focus warnings (for example that it can only be changed once).

label: Focus
summary: A short name of the game concept Education Focus, shown as the word Focus.
details: `[education_focus_short|E]` in a text shows Focus, linked to the explanation of a child's education focus. Vanilla's texts do not use this key.

label: Education trait
summary: The game concept Education Trait: the trait every character gets on becoming an adult, one of five types, each tied to a skill.
details: `[education_trait|E]` in a text shows Education Trait, linked to the concept's explanation. Its quality depends on how well the childhood trait matched the education focus and on the guardian's matching skill. It also speeds up progress in the matching lifestyle. Vanilla uses it in the education focus text and in important actions.

label: Education traits
summary: The plural form of the game concept Education Trait, shown as the words Education Traits.
details: `[education_traits|E]` in a text shows Education Traits, linked to the explanation of the traits characters get from their education at adulthood. Vanilla uses it in effect and tradition texts ("get better education traits").

label: Educations
summary: Another name of the game concept Education Focus, shown as the word Educations.
details: `[educations|E]` in a text shows Educations, linked to the explanation of the education focus. Vanilla uses it in a cultural tradition text ("a mix of both of your educations").

label: Elder
summary: The game concept Elder: a character with one or more disciples who follow their teachings.
details: `[elder|E]` in a text shows Elder, linked to the concept's explanation. An elder and a disciple gain more merit, are less likely to scheme against each other, more likely to accept and send each other friendly interactions, and both belong to the elder's movement. Vanilla uses it in effect texts ("becomes your elder").

label: Elder's
summary: The possessive form of the game concept Elder, shown as the word Elder's.
details: `[elder_possessive|E]` in a text shows Elder's, linked to the explanation of an elder (a character whose disciples follow their teachings). Vanilla's texts do not use it with `|E`.

label: Elder health traits
summary: The game concept Elder Health Traits: age-related traits characters can gain as they grow older, such as a faltering heart or fragile bones.
details: `[elder_traits|E]` in a text shows Elder Health Traits, linked to the concept's explanation. They usually appear around age 50 but can come earlier; good health and some traits make them less likely. Vanilla uses it in culture and religion texts that make these traits rarer.

label: Elderly health
summary: The game concept Elderly Health: some traits are more dangerous for characters past a certain age.
details: `[elderly_health|E]` in a text shows Elderly Health, linked to the concept's explanation. The age comes from the define `NCharacter.FEMALE_ELDERLY_AGE`. A penalty to elderly health adds to the normal health penalties, even from the same trait. Vanilla uses it as the name of the elderly health modifier.

label: Elders
summary: The plural form of the game concept Elder, shown as the word Elders.
details: `[elders|E]` in a text shows Elders, linked to the explanation of an elder (a character whose disciples follow their teachings). Vanilla uses it in a situation parameter text about independent rulers swearing fealty or paying tribute to their elders.

label: Elders'
summary: The plural possessive form of the game concept Elder, shown as the word Elders'.
details: `[elders_possessive|E]` in a text shows Elders', linked to the explanation of an elder. Vanilla uses it in a scheme text ("Your Elders' learning").

label: Election
summary: Another name of the game concept Elector, shown as the word Election.
details: `[election|E]` in a text shows Election, linked to the explanation of electors: the characters who vote for their preferred heir to a title under an elective succession law, the law deciding who counts as one. Vanilla uses it in the important action about an ongoing election in a title.

label: Elections
summary: Another name of the game concept Elector, shown as the word Elections.
details: `[elections|E]` in a text shows Elections, linked to the explanation of electors (who vote on a title's heir under elective succession). Vanilla uses it in the important action about ongoing elections in the realm.

label: Elective succession
summary: The game concept Elective Succession: electors vote on a title's next holder instead of it passing by ordinary inheritance.
details: `[elective_succession|E]` in a text shows Elective Succession, linked to the concept's explanation. Vanilla uses it in an interaction text about titles held under elective or advanced succession.

label: Elector
summary: The game concept Elector: a character who votes for their preferred heir to a title under an elective succession law.
details: `[elector|E]` in a text shows Elector, linked to the concept's explanation. Which characters are electors depends on the specific law. Vanilla uses it in faction reasons and in the nomination concept text.

label: Elector icon
summary: The election icon, an alias of the game concept Elector whose name text is the icon `@election_icon!`.
details: `[elector_i|E]` in a text shows the icon, linked to the explanation of electors (who vote on a title's heir under elective succession). Vanilla's texts do not use this key.

label: Electors
summary: The plural form of the game concept Elector, shown as the word Electors.
details: `[electors|E]` in a text shows Electors, linked to the explanation of electors. Vanilla uses it in the elective succession concept text and in a list of hook effects ("makes electors more likely to vote as you do").

label: Elephant cavalry
summary: The game concept Elephant Cavalry: mounted, often armored men-at-arms on elephants.
details: `[elephant_cavalry|E]` in a text shows Elephant Cavalry, linked to the concept's explanation. Each kind is different, but in general they counter infantry, are countered by spearmen, and are often strong in jungle terrain. Vanilla uses it as the regiment type's name and in accolade texts.

label: Eligible child
summary: The game concept Eligible Child: a child that the law allows to inherit their parent's titles.
details: `[eligible_child|E]` in a text shows Eligible Child, linked to the concept's explanation. Bastards are not eligible, and neither are children of certain genders under some gender laws. Vanilla uses it in succession law texts ("their oldest eligible child").

label: Eligible children
summary: The plural form of the game concept Eligible Child, shown as the words Eligible Children.
details: `[eligible_children|E]` in a text shows Eligible Children, linked to the explanation of children allowed to inherit their parent's titles. Vanilla uses it in the implicit claims concept text and in partition succession texts.

label: Embark
summary: Another name of the game concept Embarking, shown as the word Embark.
details: `[embark|E]` in a text shows Embark, linked to the explanation of embarking: an army boards a fleet on its own when ordered into a sea zone or when there is no land path, and pays gold per 100 men (the define `NFleet.EMBARK_GOLD_COST_PER_HUNDRED`). Vanilla uses it in the fleet tooltip ("Embark Cost") and the fleet concept text.

label: Embarkation
summary: Another name of the game concept Embarking, shown as the word Embarkation.
details: `[embarkation|E]` in a text shows Embarkation, linked to the explanation of embarking (armies boarding fleets for a gold cost). Vanilla uses it in the name of the embarkation cost modifier.

label: Embarked
summary: Another name of the game concept Embarking, shown as the word Embarked.
details: `[embarked|E]` in a text shows Embarked, linked to the explanation of embarking. Vanilla uses it for armies at sea, for example in Constantinople decisions against embarked enemy armies.

label: Embarked icon
summary: The embarked icon, an alias of the game concept Embarking whose name text is the icon `@embarked_icon!`.
details: Vanilla writes it as `[embarked_i]` without `|E`, which shows just the icon, as in the army maintenance breakdown for embarked armies; with `|E` it would link the icon to the explanation of embarking.

label: Embarking
summary: The game concept Embarking: an army boards a fleet on its own when ordered into a sea zone or when no land path leads to its target.
details: `[embarking|E]` in a text shows Embarking, linked to the concept's explanation. Embarking costs gold, standing for getting and building ships: a set amount per 100 men (the define `NFleet.EMBARK_GOLD_COST_PER_HUNDRED`). Vanilla uses it in the army view ("Embarking: ... left").

label: Embrace celibacy
summary: The game concept Embrace Celibacy: a decision that gives a character the celibate trait whenever they choose.
details: `[embrace_celibacy|E]` in a text shows Embrace Celibacy, linked to the concept's explanation. Vanilla uses it in effect texts that unlock it together with the abandon celibacy decision.

label: Embrace celibacy decision
summary: Another name of the game concept Embrace Celibacy, shown as the words Embrace Celibacy Decision.
details: `[embrace_celibacy_decision|E]` in a text shows Embrace Celibacy Decision, linked to the explanation of this decision (a character takes the celibate trait at will). Vanilla's texts do not use this key.

label: Eminent holy site
summary: The game concept Eminent Holy Site: a holy site of high importance to a faith; each faith may name only a few.
details: `[eminent_holy_site|E]` in a text shows Eminent Holy Site, linked to the concept's explanation. Only eminent holy sites give modifiers that affect all of the faith's followers. Vanilla uses it in messages about a holy site being raised to eminent.

label: Eminent
summary: A short name of the game concept Eminent Holy Site, shown as the word Eminent.
details: With `|E`, `[eminent_holy_site_short|E]` shows Eminent linked to the explanation of eminent holy sites. Vanilla writes it without `|E` in the holy site window ("(Eminent)"), which shows just the word.

label: Eminent holy sites
summary: The plural form of the game concept Eminent Holy Site, shown as the words Eminent Holy Sites.
details: `[eminent_holy_sites|E]` in a text shows Eminent Holy Sites, linked to the explanation of a faith's most important holy sites. Vanilla uses it in the holy site concept text and in holy site decisions about the maximum number.

label: Emperor
summary: The game concept Emperor: a ruler whose primary title is an empire.
details: `[emperor|E]` in a text shows Emperor, linked to the concept's explanation. An emperor ranks above kings and below hegemons, can have kings and lower rulers as vassals and only a hegemon as liege. Vanilla uses the word very often (256 uses through chains).

label: Emperors
summary: The plural form of the game concept Emperor, shown as the word Emperors.
details: `[emperors|E]` in a text shows Emperors, linked to the explanation of an emperor (a ruler whose primary title is an empire). Vanilla uses it in texts about several emperors of the same faith competing.

label: Empire
summary: The game concept Empire: a title one tier below a hegemony and one above a kingdom.
details: `[empire|E]` in a text shows Empire, linked to the concept's explanation. The holder has de jure rights to its lands and can have kings as vassals. An empire can be dormant with no holder; a ruler who controls more than 80% of its counties can then create it. Vanilla uses the word very often (155 uses through chains).

label: Empires
summary: The plural form of the game concept Empire, shown as the word Empires.
details: `[empires|E]` in a text shows Empires, linked to the explanation of an empire (the title tier between kingdom and hegemony). Vanilla uses it in decisions and in texts about empires competing for primacy.

label: End date
summary: The game concept End Date: the year 1453 AD, when the game ends.
details: `[end_date|E]` in a text shows End Date, linked to the concept's explanation. Vanilla uses it on the game over screen ("Reached the End Date").

label: Ending phase
summary: The game concept Ending Phase: a special phase of a struggle that ends the struggle when it is reached.
details: `[ending_phase|E]` in a text shows Ending Phase, linked to the concept's explanation. Involved and interloper characters move the struggle towards it in the usual way, through struggle catalysts. Vanilla uses it in struggle texts.

label: Enforce truce
summary: The game concept Enforce Truce: an interaction of rulers involved in a struggle that ends a war in a white peace (no side wins) and sets truces.
details: `[enforce_truce|E]` in a text shows Enforce Truce, linked to the concept's explanation. It only works on wars between other involved rulers of lower rank, where at least one side is independent or part of the same realm. Vanilla uses it in a struggle ending decision that unlocks it.

label: Enforced truce
summary: Another name of the game concept Enforce Truce, shown as the words Enforced Truce.
details: `[enforced_truce|E]` in a text shows Enforced Truce, linked to the explanation of this struggle interaction that ends a war in a white peace. Vanilla uses it in the interaction's texts and in a struggle catalyst ("Enforced Truce catalyst").

label: Enshrine
summary: Another name of the game concept Enshrined, shown as the word Enshrine.
details: `[enshrine|E]` in a text shows Enshrine, linked to the explanation of enshrined relics: a holy relic placed in a holy site turns on and improves the site's bonuses. Vanilla uses it in the faith view and important actions ("Select ... Artifact(s) to enshrine").

label: Enshrined
summary: The game concept Enshrined: a holy relic placed in a holy site, which turns on the site's bonuses and makes them stronger.
details: `[enshrined|E]` in a text shows Enshrined, linked to the concept's explanation. The boost grows with the total rarity of all enshrined artifacts. An enshrined artifact belongs to no character any more and no longer decays, but the site's holder, top liege or clerical region holder can act on it. Only relics of your own faith help; others give nothing. Vanilla uses it in the holy site window ("Enshrined Artifacts").

label: Entourage
summary: The game concept Entourage: everyone who travels with a character and shares the journey's challenges.
details: `[entourage|E]` in a text shows Entourage, linked to the concept's explanation. The travel leader court position leads it and manages the travel plans. Some characters join by default when travel is planned; travel and activity options add more. Vanilla uses it in effect texts for recruiting someone into the entourage.

label: Entrant
summary: The game concept Entrant: a character taking part in the imperial examination activity.
details: `[entrant|E]` in a text shows Entrant, linked to the concept's explanation. Vanilla uses it in list texts ("Every entrant").

label: Entrants
summary: The plural form of the game concept Entrant, shown as the word Entrants.
details: `[entrants|E]` in a text shows Entrants, linked to the explanation of the imperial examination's participants. Vanilla uses it in the examination's texts about how much merit how many entrants get.

label: Entrenched regencies
summary: The plural form of the game concept Entrenched Regency, shown as the words Entrenched Regencies.
details: `[entrenched_regencies|E]` in a text shows Entrenched Regencies, linked to the explanation of regencies that lasted so long that the regent grew much stronger. Vanilla uses it in a diarchy text about dismissing them with a gift.

label: Entrenched regency
summary: The game concept Entrenched Regency: a regency that has lasted too long, making the regent even stronger compared to their liege.
details: `[entrenched_regency|E]` in a text shows Entrenched Regency, linked to the concept's explanation. The regent's benefits from the scales of power become much stronger. It ends when the regent accepts a gift from the liege, or when the liege tips the scales in their own favor. Vanilla uses it in the regency concept text and accolades.

label: Entrench
summary: Another name of the game concept Entrenched Regency, shown as the word Entrench.
details: `[entrenched_regency_entrench|E]` in a text shows Entrench, linked to the explanation of entrenched regencies. Vanilla uses it as a verb: diarchs can entrench their regency, becoming harder to remove.

label: Entrenched
summary: Another name of the game concept Entrenched Regency, shown as the word Entrenched.
details: `[entrenched_regency_entrenched|E]` in a text shows Entrenched, linked to the explanation of entrenched regencies (regents grown much stronger after a long regency). Vanilla's texts do not use this key.

label: Regency
summary: Another name of the game concept Entrenched Regency, shown as the word Regency.
details: `[entrenched_regency_regency|E]` in a text shows the word Regency, but it links to the explanation of the entrenched regency, not of regencies in general. Vanilla's texts do not use this key.

label: Entrenched regent
summary: Another name of the game concept Entrenched Regency, shown as the words Entrenched Regent.
details: `[entrenched_regent|E]` in a text shows Entrenched Regent, linked to the explanation of entrenched regencies. Vanilla uses it in the co-monarch concept text and in an interaction reason ("Entrenched Regent Protects Realm").

label: Entrenched regents
summary: Another name of the game concept Entrenched Regency, shown as the words Entrenched Regents.
details: `[entrenched_regents|E]` in a text shows Entrenched Regents, linked to the explanation of entrenched regencies. Vanilla's texts do not use this key.

label: Become adventurer decision
summary: The game concept for the Become Adventurer decision: a ruler of a small realm gives up their lands of their own will and becomes an adventurer.
details: `[ep3_become_landless_adventurer_decision|E]` in a text shows the decision's name followed by "Decision", linked to the concept's explanation. Certain cultural traditions unlock the decision. Vanilla's texts do not use this key.

label: Adventurer invasion
summary: The game concept for the Adventurer Invasion casus belli: it lets an adventurer declare war to carve out a new realm.
details: `[ep3_laamp_adventurer_invasion_war|E]` in a text shows the war's name, Adventurer Invasion, linked to the concept's explanation. Vanilla's texts do not use this key.

label: Negotiate settlement
summary: The game concept for the Negotiate Settlement interaction: a ruler lets an unruly adventurer settle in their realm.
details: `[ep3_negotiate_settlement_interaction|E]` in a text shows the interaction's name, Negotiate Settlement, linked to the concept's explanation. Vanilla's texts do not use this key.

label: Purchase land
summary: The game concept for the Purchase Land interaction: an adventurer buys land from a ruler and settles in their realm.
details: `[ep3_purchase_land_interaction|E]` in a text shows the interaction's name, Purchase Land, linked to the concept's explanation. Vanilla's texts do not use this key.

label: Plague
summary: The game concept Plague: a disease outbreak that spreads across the map, harming the places it reaches and infecting the characters living there.
details: In a text, `[epidemic|E]` shows the word "Plague" linked to the concept's explanation. Each affected barony has an infection rate that sets how bad it is there; plague resistance works against it. A plague also has an intensity that decides how far it spreads, how long it lasts and how many die. Vanilla uses it in decision, message filter and concept texts.

label: Plague
summary: Another name of the game concept Plague: it shows the plague icon instead of a word.
details: The game's text for this name is the plague icon (`@epidemic_icon!`), so a text that writes `[epidemic_i]` shows that icon. Vanilla uses it as the prefix of plague modifiers. The concept itself is a disease outbreak that spreads across the map and infects characters.

label: Plague resistance
summary: Another name of the game concept Plague Resistance: the short form "Plague Res.", for how well a barony or county holds out against plagues.
details: In a text, `[epidemic_res|E]` shows "Plague Res." linked to the concept's explanation. Vanilla uses it as the label in the holding view. Plague resistance lowers the infection rate of a barony or county.

label: Plague resistance
summary: The game concept Plague Resistance: how well a barony or county holds out against plagues; it lowers their infection rate.
details: In a text, `[epidemic_resistance|E]` shows "Plague Resistance" linked to the concept's explanation. It can be raised by buildings (such as hospices or burial sites), by the court physician's court position task, by decisions and by events. Vanilla uses it in court position and decision texts.

label: Plague
summary: Another name of the game concept Plague, in the plural: disease outbreaks that spread across the map and infect characters.
details: In a text, `[epidemics|E]` shows "Plagues" linked to the concept's explanation. Vanilla uses it in decision, tradition and concept texts.

label: Nickname
summary: Another name of the game concept Nickname: a second name a character takes or is given, such as Charles 'the Bald'.
details: In a text, `[epithet|E]` shows "Epithet" linked to the concept's explanation. Nicknames are only for show; bad ones can be replaced by good ones later. Vanilla uses it in the nickname events.

label: Nickname
summary: Another name of the game concept Nickname, in the plural: second names characters take or are given.
details: In a text, `[epithets|E]` shows "Epithets" linked to the concept's explanation. No vanilla text uses this name.

label: Fertility equilibrium
summary: Another name of the game concept Fertility Equilibrium: the level a county's fertility moves towards over time.
details: In a text, `[equilibrium|E]` shows "Equilibrium" linked to the concept's explanation. A county's fertility grows while it is below this level and falls while above it; the level depends mostly on the county's growth and consumption modifiers. Vanilla uses it in the county fertility tooltip.

label: Era
summary: The game concept Era: the stage of a culture's progress that decides which innovations it can discover.
details: In a text, `[era|E]` shows "Era" linked to the concept's explanation. A new era can only begin after a certain year and once at least half of the previous era's innovations are discovered. Tribal and nomadic rulers can only use tribal era innovations. Vanilla uses it in court position salary texts and elsewhere.

label: Era
summary: Another name of the game concept Era, in the plural: the stages of a culture's progress that decide which innovations it can discover.
details: In a text, `[eras|E]` shows "Eras" linked to the concept's explanation. Vanilla uses it in concept and tutorial texts about innovations.

label: Escalated peasant faction
summary: The game concept Escalated Peasant Faction: a dangerous faction of unhappy counties that already forced a peasant faction's demands on a vassal and can break away from the realm.
details: In a text, `[escalated_peasant_faction|E]` shows "Escalated Peasant Faction" linked to the concept's explanation. Its members are counties with low county opinion, and it has a notorious leader. Vanilla uses it in faction texts and a domicile building parameter.

label: Escalated peasant faction
summary: Another name of the game concept Escalated Peasant Faction, in the plural: dangerous factions of unhappy counties that can break away from the realm.
details: In a text, `[escalated_peasant_factions|E]` shows "Escalated Peasant Factions" linked to the concept's explanation. No vanilla text uses this name.

label: Find secrets
summary: The game concept Find Secrets: the spymaster's councillor task that targets a ruler's court and tries to uncover secrets of the characters there.
details: In a text, `[espionage|E]` shows "Find Secrets" linked to the concept's explanation. Vanilla uses it in effect texts, for example that the task may also fabricate hooks.

label: Estate
summary: The game concept Estate: a domicile held by the house head of a notable noble family in an administrative realm, a private landholding not tied to any landed title.
details: In a text, `[estate|E]` shows "Estate" linked to the concept's explanation. Estate buildings can be built there to add to the family's wealth and influence, and the estate passes on to later generations. Vanilla uses it in government, message and core texts.

label: Estate building
summary: The game concept Estate Building: a lasting improvement built on a noble family's estate.
details: In a text, `[estate_building|E]` shows "Estate Building" linked to the concept's explanation. The estate's owner builds them to earn private income, grow the family's influence and unlock decisions, interactions and more. Vanilla uses it in tradition and modifier texts, for example cost reductions.

label: Estate building
summary: Another name of the game concept Estate Building, in the plural: lasting improvements built on a noble family's estate.
details: In a text, `[estate_buildings|E]` shows "Estate Buildings" linked to the concept's explanation. Vanilla uses it in core, message and concept texts.

label: Estate
summary: Another name of the game concept Estate, in the plural: the private landholdings of noble families in administrative realms.
details: In a text, `[estates|E]` shows "Estates" linked to the concept's explanation. Vanilla uses it in court position and ruler designer texts.

label: Ethos
summary: The game concept Ethos: a culture's core values and outlook on life.
details: In a text, `[ethos|E]` shows "Ethos" linked to the concept's explanation. The ethos strongly affects what it costs the culture head to set up new traditions. Vanilla uses it in court type and decision texts.

label: Exam advantage
summary: The game concept Exam Advantage: a bonus that raises a character's chances in the actions of an imperial examination, such as answering questions.
details: In a text, `[exam_advantage|E]` shows "Exam Advantage" linked to the concept's explanation. Vanilla uses it in legacy, scheme and examination event texts that grant one.

label: Exam cheat
summary: The game concept Exam Cheat: something that unlocks options to get around the coming exam, at a high cost if the cheater is caught.
details: In a text, `[exam_cheat|E]` shows "Exam Cheat" linked to the concept's explanation. Vanilla uses it in imperial examination event texts where a character gains one.

label: Exam score
summary: The game concept Exam Score: the score that decides how likely an entrant is to pass an imperial examination.
details: In a text, `[exam_score|E]` shows "Exam Score" linked to the concept's explanation. The starting score comes from the entrant's education trait and their learning, stewardship or martial skill, depending on the exam's focus. Vanilla uses it in examination events that raise the score.

label: Civil service examination
summary: Another name of the game concept Civil Service Examination: the exams through which bureaucratic governments appoint officials by merit rather than birth.
details: In a text, `[examination|E]` shows "Examination" linked to the concept's explanation. Through them, scholars of any birth can gain governorship appointments, and vanilla's merit texts tie the higher merit levels to passing the exams. Vanilla uses it in merit and decision texts.

label: Civil service examination
summary: Another name of the game concept Civil Service Examination, in the plural: the exams through which bureaucratic governments appoint officials by merit.
details: In a text, `[examinations|E]` shows "Examinations" linked to the concept's explanation. Vanilla uses it in important action and merit texts.

label: Exceptional epic
summary: The game concept Exceptional Epic: a family epic from the Commission Epic decision that turned out exceptional and gives bigger bonuses than a normal one.
details: In a text, `[exceptional_epic|E]` shows "Exceptional Epic" linked to the concept's explanation. Event choices can change the chance of an exceptional epic; vanilla uses it in the commission epic events to show that chance.

label: Excommunication
summary: Another name of the game concept Excommunication, as the verb: a head of faith casting a character out, so that others of that faith see them as a criminal.
details: In a text, `[excommunicate|E]` shows "Excommunicate" linked to the concept's explanation. Vanilla uses it in interaction texts that petition a head of faith.

label: Excommunication
summary: Another name of the game concept Excommunication, as the state: a character cast out by their head of faith.
details: In a text, `[excommunicated|E]` shows "Excommunicated" linked to the concept's explanation. Vanilla uses it in texts of the war that dissolves an excommunicated emperor's empire.

label: Recover from excommunication
summary: The game concept Recover from Excommunication: what an excommunicated character suffers at once and while it lasts, until they are absolved.
details: In a text, `[excommunicated_recovery|E]` shows "Recover from Excommunication" linked to the concept's explanation. On excommunication the character loses much legitimacy and one piety level and gains half as much piety while the trait remains. Vanilla uses it in a tenet text that makes absolution cheaper.

label: Excommunicated ruler
summary: The game concept Excommunicated Ruler: the excommunicated ruler whom the attackers in an excommunication war fight to remove from power.
details: In a text, `[excommunicated_ruler|E]` shows "Excommunicated Ruler" linked to the concept's explanation. If the attackers win, they gain much piety and their head of faith's approval, and the ruler must abdicate to their heir; if the ruler wins, the excommunication is lifted. No vanilla text uses this name.

label: Excommunication
summary: The game concept Excommunication: being cast out by one's head of faith, so that other characters of that faith see one as a criminal.
details: In a text, `[excommunication|E]` shows "Excommunication" linked to the concept's explanation. An excommunicated independent ruler can face an excommunication war and must abdicate if they lose. It can be lifted by repenting, petitioning the head of faith or winning such a war. Vanilla uses it in AI personality and interaction texts.

label: Excommunicated ruler
summary: Another name of the game concept Excommunicated Ruler: the excommunication war, fought to remove an excommunicated ruler from power.
details: In a text, `[excommunication_war|E]` shows "Excommunication War" linked to the concept's explanation. If the attackers win, the ruler must abdicate to their heir; if the ruler wins, the excommunication is lifted. Vanilla uses it in concept texts about abdication and excommunication.

label: Execute
summary: The game concept Execute: putting an imprisoned character to death.
details: In a text, `[execute|E]` shows "Execute" linked to the concept's explanation. It counts as tyranny unless the imprisoner has an execution reason. Executions raise the executioner's dread, and the victim's close family always dislike it. Vanilla uses it in AI personality and other texts.

label: Execution reason
summary: The game concept Execution Reason: a reason that lets a liege execute a subject held in their dungeon without it counting as tyranny.
details: In a text, `[execute_reason|E]` shows "Execution Reason" linked to the concept's explanation. It usually comes from the subject being a criminal.

label: Execution reason
summary: Another name of the game concept Execution Reason, in the plural: reasons that let a liege freely execute an imprisoned subject.
details: In a text, `[execute_reasons|E]` shows "Execution Reasons" linked to the concept's explanation.

label: Execute
summary: Another name of the game concept Execute, as "executed": an imprisoned character put to death.
details: In a text, `[executed|E]` shows "Executed" linked to the concept's explanation.

label: Execute
summary: Another name of the game concept Execute, as "executing": putting an imprisoned character to death.
details: In a text, `[executing|E]` shows "Executing" linked to the concept's explanation.

label: Execute
summary: Another name of the game concept Execute, as the noun: the putting to death of an imprisoned character.
details: In a text, `[execution|E]` shows "Execution" linked to the concept's explanation.

label: Execute
summary: Another name of the game concept Execute, in the plural noun: executions of imprisoned characters.
details: In a text, `[executions|E]` shows "Executions" linked to the concept's explanation.

label: Existing development
summary: The game concept Existing Development: the penalty on the steward's Develop County task, which grows the more development a county already has.
details: In a text, `[existing_development|E]` shows "Existing Development" linked to the concept's explanation. By default the penalty is at its largest from 10 development; an innovation of each era raises that limit. Vanilla uses it in council task texts.

label: Expand dominance
summary: The game concept Expand Dominance: a special war of nomadic rulers, either for land within their de jure area or to push that area into new frontiers.
details: In a text, `[expand_dominance|E]` shows "Expand Dominance" linked to the concept's explanation. Nomadic rulers of duchy tier or higher can start it within their de jure lands.

label: Expansion decree
summary: Another name of the game concept Expansion Decree: a mandala decree that has all subjects work on expanding the realm.
details: In a text, `[expansion_decree|E]` shows "Expansion" linked to the concept's explanation. Under it, raising soldiers, military accommodations and supporting the mandala ruler's wars come first. Vanilla uses it in decision texts and next to the other mandala decrees.

label: Expected legitimacy
summary: The game concept Expected Legitimacy: the legitimacy level a ruler's vassals expect of them, based on their history together.
details: In a text, `[expected_legitimacy|E]` shows "Expected Legitimacy" linked to the concept's explanation. Being the vassal's de jure liege, part of their close family or the preferred heir are among the things that lower the expectation.

label: Lifestyle experience
summary: Another name of the game concept Lifestyle Experience: the points a character gathers in a lifestyle, from their chosen focus or from events.
details: In a text, `[experience|E]` shows "Experience" linked to the concept's explanation. Each lifestyle has its own experience; enough of it earns a perk. Vanilla uses it in focus and decision texts.

label: Extended family
summary: The game concept Extended Family: a character's cousins, uncles, aunts, nephews and nieces.
details: In a text, `[extended_family|E]` shows "Extended Family" linked to the concept's explanation. Together with the close family it makes up a character's family.

label: Extended family
summary: Another name of the game concept Extended Family: the members of a character's extended family (cousins, uncles, aunts, nephews and nieces).
details: In a text, `[extended_family_members|E]` shows "Extended Family Members" linked to the concept's explanation.

label: Clerical ruler puppet
summary: The game concept Clerical Ruler Puppet: a powerful cleric, such as an archbishop or even the head of faith, who has become another ruler's puppet.
details: In a text, `[external_clerical_puppet|E]` shows "Clerical Ruler Puppet" linked to the concept's explanation. The mightier the cleric, the more the puppet master can do: a puppet head of faith can excommunicate enemies, appoint cardinals, grant a pressed claim or start a holy war.

label: Clerical ruler puppet
summary: Another name of the game concept Clerical Ruler Puppet, in the plural: powerful clerics who have become another ruler's puppets.
details: In a text, `[external_clerical_puppets|E]` shows "Clerical Ruler Puppets" linked to the concept's explanation.

label: Secular ruler puppet
summary: The game concept Secular Ruler Puppet: a ruler outside the clergy who has become another character's puppet.
details: In a text, `[external_ruler_puppet|E]` shows "Secular Ruler Puppet" linked to the concept's explanation. Through such a puppet one can meddle in other realms, for example with schemes or imprisonment; getting one has conditions the concept lists.

label: Secular ruler puppet
summary: Another name of the game concept Secular Ruler Puppet, in the plural: non-clergy rulers who have become another character's puppets.
details: In a text, `[external_ruler_puppets|E]` shows "Secular Ruler Puppets" linked to the concept's explanation.

label: Extort subjects decision
summary: Another name of the game concept Extort Subjects Decision: a decision with several ways to squeeze extra gold out of one's subjects, each with its own cost.
details: In a text, `[extort_subjects|E]` shows "Extort Subjects" linked to the concept's explanation.

label: Extort subjects decision
summary: The game concept Extort Subjects Decision: a decision with several ways to squeeze extra gold out of one's subjects, each with its own cost.
details: In a text, `[extort_subjects_decision|E]` shows "Extort Subjects Decision" linked to the concept's explanation. No vanilla text uses this name.

label: Extramarital sex
summary: The game concept Extramarital Sex: sex outside marriage, with consequences when it is found out that depend on the faith's doctrines.
details: In a text, `[extramarital_sex|E]` shows "Extramarital Sex" linked to the concept's explanation. If discovered, each of the two becomes known as a fornicator or an adulterer, depending on the case. No vanilla text uses this name.

label: Extramarital sex
summary: Another name of the game concept Extramarital Sex: the words "sleeping with", linked to that concept.
details: In a text, `[extramarital_sex_sleeping_with|E]` shows "sleeping with" linked to the explanation of extramarital sex. Vanilla uses it in the seduce scheme's text.

label: Fabricate claim on county
summary: The game concept Fabricate Claim on County: the court chaplain's councillor task that works on a county and, at full progress, lets you fabricate a claim on it for gold.
details: In a text, `[fabricate_claim|E]` shows "Fabricate Claim on County" linked to the concept's explanation. Progress builds up over time until it reaches 100%.

label: Fabricate claim on county
summary: Another name of the game concept Fabricate Claim on County, in short: the court chaplain's task that leads to a fabricated claim on a county.
details: In a text, `[fabricate_claim_short|E]` shows "Fabricate Claim" linked to the concept's explanation.

label: Fabricate claim on county
summary: Another name of the game concept Fabricate Claim on County: claims made through that court chaplain task.
details: In a text, `[fabricated_claims_short|E]` shows "Fabricated Claims" linked to the concept's explanation.

label: Fabricate claim on county
summary: Another name of the game concept Fabricate Claim on County, as "fabricating claims": the court chaplain's work towards a claim on a county.
details: In a text, `[fabricating_claims|E]` shows "Fabricating Claims" linked to the concept's explanation.

label: Faction
summary: The game concept Faction: a group of vassals with shared political aims; for some kinds, such as the peasant faction, the people of counties can join too.
details: In a text, `[faction|E]` shows "Faction" linked to the concept's explanation. A faction becomes dangerous when its discontent gets high enough and it sends its liege an ultimatum. Vanilla uses it in many texts.

label: Faction commitment
summary: The game concept Faction Commitment: how likely a character is to back a faction against their liege.
details: In a text, `[faction_commitment|E]` shows "Faction Commitment" linked to the concept's explanation. Many things affect it, most often personality, opinion and culture.

label: Discontent
summary: The game concept Discontent: how close a faction is to sending its ultimatum.
details: In a text, `[faction_discontent|E]` shows "Discontent" linked to the concept's explanation. It rises each month while the faction's military power is at the threshold and falls while it is below; very strong factions grow discontent fast.

label: Imperial policy faction
summary: Another name of the game concept Imperial Policy Faction: a faction that wants to change the realm's imperial policy to a new law its leader picks.
details: In a text, `[faction_imperial_policy|E]` shows "Imperial Policy" linked to the concept's explanation. No vanilla text uses this name.

label: Independence faction
summary: Another name of the game concept Independence Faction: a faction that wants independence for all its members from their liege.
details: In a text, `[faction_independence|E]` shows "Independence" linked to the concept's explanation. If it succeeds, its members become independent. Vanilla uses it in a language concept text.

label: Liberty faction
summary: Another name of the game concept Liberty Faction: a faction that wants lower government authority and, where they apply, better vassal contracts for its members.
details: In a text, `[faction_liberty|E]` shows "Liberty" linked to the concept's explanation. If it succeeds, the liege cannot change the realm's government authority for a while. No vanilla text uses this name.
